summary.headline: Dynamic Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to a record Q1 level, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore and order book at INR811 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record first-quarter revenue, up 33% YoY, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore (margin 10.9%) and PAT up 37% to INR25 crore. Growth was largely price-driven: volume grew only 5-6% against a high base of roughly 25-26% last year, as aluminium price spikes led to order postponements in April-May. The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.

segments.name: HV cables
segments.commentary: 68% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Core growth driver alongside T&D demand.

segments.name: LV cables
segments.commentary: 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Company has been moving mix away from LV toward HV and MV.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: 2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Conductor volume growth was lower than cable volume growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Solar / renewable cables
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue in Q1; expected to remain in a similar range for FY27 H1, rising in H2 as new plant comes on. Management sees 25-30% growth for the next 3-4 years.

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: Temporarily held back due to weak margins and competition; not a shutdown. Zero contribution in last Q1, so no base effect this quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 13% of revenue. US contributed about 15% of exports in its first quarter; Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa remain the core; Middle East negligible.

guidance_outlook: No formal annual guidance; management reiterated 18-20% growth record over the last 10-15 years and aims to sustain a similar long-term rate, with some quarters of higher, others of moderate growth.
New plant (about INR45 crore capex) to commission from September 2026; meaningful revenue expected only from Q4 FY27.
Target optimum utilisation of 80-85% of the new plant by end FY28, roughly 18 months from commencement.
Asset turnover of 6-7x on the new plant implies revenue addition; brownfield expansion possible later.
Solar cable revenue share to stay around 20% for FY27; more notable increase next year.
US market: margins initially similar to domestic, with possible incremental margins later; no one-year target given.
capex_capacity: New plant: capex about INR45 crore, commissioning from September 2026 (delay behind, on track per management).
E-beam technology is new; will be launched first at the new facility.

HTLS conductor and data centre cable products: management says most capex is fungible with existing machinery, with limited add-on capex needed; focus is on product development and customer approvals.
Licensed for HV/LV and MV cables for the US market.
demand_pricing: Price variation clause in variable-price contracts passes input cost changes to customers; fixed-price contracts are hedged by booking raw material at order time (about 20% of order book is fixed-price).
Order book of INR811 crore; April-May order inflow was weak as customers resisted booking at elevated aluminium prices; orders now limited to near-term (2-4 month) execution.
Order cycles and order sizes have shortened due to global volatility and tariffs; management says dispatches not impacted.
Competition described as healthy for now despite capacity expansion across the industry; demand picking up with expansion.
US market is distribution-led; competition is global (US local makers, Mexico, Turkey, India, China). Management cites large replacement demand over 10-20 years.
Management says some Adani/Birla cable business is for captive use; Birla focused on house wires; sees low risk to orders from these groups.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting margins if copper and aluminium costs stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable-price contracts carry a clause passing input cost changes to customers; for fixed-price orders, raw material is booked at order time to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of Q1 volume and realisation growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 5-6% YoY; most of the balance of revenue growth came from aluminium-driven price increases. Base effect was high at about 25-26% volume growth last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weaker in Q1 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect, plus customer order postponements after a sharp input price rise in March-May. Management expects improvement as prices settle but calls the environment very uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new plant on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, regulatory delays are behind; commissioning planned for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book only about 10% up YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers were reluctant to book at elevated prices in April-May; weak order booking was industry-wide and should pick up as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US export opportunity and business model?
qa_highlights.answer: First US supplies started this quarter after 15-18 months of work on licences and tariffs; US contributed about 15% of exports. Model is distributor-led, with HV/LV and MV cables licensed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off and full-year guidance position?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the high growth came from price increases. No annual guidance, but long-term growth of 18-20% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the new capex add and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; target 80-85% utilisation by end FY28; asset turnover 6-7x on INR45 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing competition intensifying from capacity expansions?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is currently healthy; demand is rising in step with industry expansion, and the T&D story is seen as secular.

qa_highlights.question: Why was debt higher versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory value rose 20-25% due to higher raw material prices (quantity unchanged); receivables comparison on last-six-month sales is unchanged in debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company diversifying into house wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the B2B building wire segment, not B2C distribution or branding; positioned as an additional product in similar segments.

risks_watch: Order book growth slowed to about 10% YoY, and order cycles have shortened; watch Q2 order inflows as prices settle.
Volume growth of 5-6% against a high base; watch whether volume recovers as management expects.
Commodity price volatility: inventory values rose, raising debt; watch working capital and borrowing costs.
Commissioning slippage risk for the September 2026 plant; ramp to 80-85% utilisation by end FY28 is targeted, not assured.
US export ramp is at an early stage; reorders and cross-referencing not yet proven.
Railway signalling business held back; re-entry timing unclear.
Industry-wide capacity additions in HV/EHV could pressure pricing later.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, solar and export opportunities, but cautious on near-term volumes and order inflows, which management attributed to raw material price volatility and customer reluctance. Responses on the US plan, HTLS and data centre timelines were deliberately non-specific.
